why: The canonical XOR fact: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, and XOR is order-independent, so XOR-ing the whole array cancels every pair and leaves the single value, in O(1) space.
hints: A hash set works. Can you do it with one integer of extra memory?
What is a ^ a? What is a ^ 0? Does the order of XOR operations matter?
acc = 0; for v in nums: acc ^= v; return acc. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Negative values work too: XOR acts on the two's-complement bits.
Sorting works but costs O(n log n); summing with a set uses O(n) memory.
